Hi Asha / Daniel —

Thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap of what I heard and next steps so we stay aligned: 

Pain points we discussed:
- Latency spikes during peak clinical hours (p90 ~450ms, goal is <200ms for inference).
- Need full data isolation and PHI controls (on-premise/VPC, dedicated GPUs, KMS).
- Predictable throughput requirement: ~500 inference requests/minute steady with 2x burst.
- Concern about cost predictability and auto-scaling behavior during large batch processing.

Goals / success criteria:
- Dedicated reserved capacity (SLA-backed) with private networking.
- P90 inference latency consistently <200ms for 4k token prompts at target load.
- Audit-ready logs and SOC 2 evidence for security/compliance reviewers.

Proposed technical direction (high level):
- Reserved pool: 4x A100-80GB equivalent GPUs (dedicated) to start, with configured autoscale policy for burst to additional reserved or preemptible capacity.
- Private deployment: VPC peering + customer-managed KMS for keys; audit logs forwarded to your SIEM.
- Fallback policy: smaller quantized model variant for non-critical throughput bursts to preserve latency SLOs while lowering cost.

Attachments I mentioned: capacity estimate and our SOC 2 summary (attached).
- 20260525-aurora-capacity-estimate.xlsx (capacity + cost breakout)
- redwood-soc2-audit-summary.pdf (SOC 2 highlights we discussed)

Next steps / asks:
1) Confirm the throughput and SLOs above or provide updated numbers by EOD Wednesday so our engineering team can finalize sizing.
2) I'll loop in Rishi (SE) and Vivek (Solutions) for a technical review and proposed config (we expect to have a proposal within 48 hours once sizing is finalized).
3) If procurement wants a PO template we can share a draft (I attached a template we typically use).

Would love a quick reply with any corrections to the recap. If this looks right, can we lock a follow-up technical review on Thursday at 10am PT?

Hi team —

Following up with a technical proposal based on Marissa / Asha's notes. Key items below; attached is a short proposal PDF with cost modeling and scaling behavior.

Summary of recommended config:
- Reserved pool: 4 x A100-80GB equiv GPUs (reserved) dedicated to Aurora tenant.
- Autoscale / burst: policy to add up to 2 additional reserved GPUs from held buffer within 30s for sustained load; allow ephemeral burst into quantized variants (4-bit) for non-critical requests.
- Network & isolation: dedicated VPC with private peering; no internet-facing ingress to inference nodes; customer-managed KMS for model keys and encryption-at-rest.
- Latency targets: p95 250ms target achievable for 4k-token prompts on the reserved pool with aggressive async batching disabled for clinical paths (we recommend sync serving for critical flows). P90 <200ms is possible if we increase to 6 reserved GPUs or tune model parallelism — tradeoff is ~18% higher monthly cost.
- PHI handling: store-and-forward not persisted in shared caches; optional prefix-KV encryption and a configurable TTL to ensure no long-term retention. We forward full audit logs to your SIEM via secure syslog endpoint.

Operational SLAs and runbook highlights:
- SLA: 99.9% uptime for reserved pool, 99% for burst capacity.
- Incident escalation: 24/7 support with a dedicated escalation contact for P1s; runbook included in attached.
- Maintenance windows: can be configured during your low-usage window (we suggested 00:00-03:00 PT).

Attachments: dedicated_capacity_proposal.pdf (detailed sizing + cost matrices)

Next steps (technical):
- Marissa: confirm final throughput numbers including nightly batch windows (Asha).
- Aurora: confirm whether p95 250ms is acceptable or if you want to pursue p90 200ms (we can provide delta-cost).
- If approved, we will prepare an SOW + preliminary PO for procurement.

Happy to jump on a short deep-dive Thursday 10am PT.
